items.label: June 1927
items.sum: Report of the R.W.A. Junior road walking championship over 10 miles at Sheffield, won by T. W. Green from A. L. Fletcher, with Belgrave beaten in the team event by Attercliffe Walking Club, and a list of Belgrave finishers.
items.s: THE R W.A. JUNIOR. Report of the R.W.A. Junior road walking championship over 10 miles at Sheffield, won by T. W. Green from A. L. Fletcher, with Belgrave beaten in the team event by Attercliffe Walking Club, and a list of Belgrave finishers. If the eagerly anticipated Road Walking "Junior" Championship at Sheffield failed to provide the expected success to the Club in the team event, ample consolation was forthcoming for any disappointment by the really great performances of T. W. Green and A. L. Fletcher who finished first and second respectively in the actual race after as good and exciting a race as has been witnessed over 10 miles. With a field of over 200 there was naturally some bunching at the start but at a mile Green was ahead with Fletcher behind a pack in close attendance. Shortly after the two drew out clear ahead and at 4½ miles Green had a nominal lead of some 2[illegible] yards. Scamell was next for the Club, 15th, then came the versatile S L King, 25th, Carne 41st, and no others in the first 60. A total of the scores of the expected prominent Clubs showed Herne Hill with 66 points, Sheffield 75, Belgrave 82 and Surrey W C. 118, which seemed fairly satisfactory until it was noted that some small numbers were showing prominently and another hasty calculation showed that the hitherto unknown quantity, the Attercliffe Walking Club had 4 in 22 and scored 40 The team race was already over bar accidents. Another mile or so and Green and Fletcher were still ahead, a yard apart. Purves of the Y.M.C.A. had moved up into 3rd position displacing the first Attercliffe man who had dropped back 5th. Their 2nd man was back to 9th and their team score now 46. Herne Hill were down to 58, Sheffield 72, and ourselves 76. The leaders were picked up again at 8½ miles when the first man to appear was Purves—running. Our pair were still forcing the pace and had gone away a little from the others. Scamell was now 16th, King 23rd and Rathbone, now walking wonderfully well, was our fourth man. Our fate in the team race was now sealed. Attercliffe were down to 36, Herne Hill 48 and Sheffield 54. We scored 69 but hearing rumours of disqualifications hoped on, but in vain. Meanwhile Green and Fletcher were having a battle royal and knowing the speed at Fletcher's command we were considering that he would be certain to win when the time came for the final effort, but Green was a sturdy finisher and resisting all challenges held on to win a very fine race by some 6 yards. In the final stages Rathbone passed King and was third home for the Club R E Wills of our 'B' team walked really well to get inside 90 minutes Saunders continues to improve and should be a useful man next year. Probably the 4 hours train journey upset the form of some, especially Knifton who had the disturbing experience of travelling by the wrong train. We started 17 and all finished as follows. T. items.label: June 1927
items.sum: Short note on the South of Thames Championship at Reading and the Southern at Farningham, where H. E. Footer's tenth place was the best by a club member in that championship.
items.s: Short note on the South of Thames Championship at Reading and the Southern at Farningham, where H. E. Footer's tenth place was the best by a club member in that championship. We have not discussed the South of Thames Championship at Reading or the Southern at Farningham. Of the first, the least said the better for as it has been said before, the train, by which we travelled, passed through Slough—"the despond" came later The race at Farningham was more satisfactory to us though the weather was not Footer put up a very fine performance here and in finishing tenth has recorded the best performance by a Club member in this Championship Footer Footer 10th in the Southern at Farningham, best by a club member in this championship South of Thames Championship Southern Cross Country Championships Reading Farningham Slough

items.s: THE BRIGHTON RELAY. Report on the "News of the World" London to Brighton relay of April 9th, 1927, where Belgrave did worse than the year before, with a stage-by-stage table of Belgrave times compared with 1926. The much discussed and eagerly anticipated "News of the World" Relay Race, held on April 9th, in the most deplorable climatic conditions, failed to bring us the expected consolation for an unfortunate experience in last year's race. In view of the fact that on paper our team was relatively stronger, and by comparison with our running in the eliminating trials held at Mitcham, our actual performance in the race was depressing to all concerned One critic said "disgusting" but we think "disappointing" more aptly sums up the position. Our troubles actually commenced at Westminster when "Micky" Pyer reported a "crocked" leg and his inability to run, but this by no means fully accounted for the fact that our performance was actually worse than that of last year. As in that race, we were nicely placed up to the end of the fourth relay but then the middle stages lost much valuable ground that could never be recovered. The performance of A. E. Smith, who made third fastest time on his relay (beaten only by the Hallamshire and Herne Hill runners) stands out as the most meritorious. The appended details will probably be of interest and will indicate more clearly the whole of the running The second column of figures represents the comparison of member's time with other competitors on the same relay. items.label: June 1927
items.sum: Report and handicap result of the club 20 mile walking championship for the President's Shield, a trial for the "National", won by E. G. Cooper from T. W. Green and S. Manning.
items.s: R. W. RICKETT'S SHIELD RACE. Report and handicap result of the club 20 mile walking championship for the President's Shield, a trial for the "National", won by E. G. Cooper from T. W. Green and S. Manning. The greater attraction of the Brighton Relay left but a small body of officials to carry out the Club 20 Mile Walking Championship for the Presidents Shield, which race intended as a trial for the "National" should have been of more than ordinary interest in view of serious gaps in the ranks of our distance walkers and of the first appearance of H. F. King over the distance and of T. W. Green, the "Junior" champion, who was expected to go close. Fortunately the worst of the weather had passed when a small field of eleven started. King and Green forced the pace followed by F. Rickard (holder for the three previous years) and E. G. Cooper. This order was maintained for some 7 miles the leaders going further and further away until the question arose "How long can they last" Rickard finished at 8 miles but he obviously was not fit Green and King were still together and passed in 65 m. 10 secs. Cooper followed, 67.59, then came Rathbone 69 4 and Manning 72 22. At 13 miles King was in trouble and retired shortly after. At 14 miles Green showed 1-53-19, Cooper 1-56-41, Rathbone 2-0-30 and Manning 2-4-25 The writer, at this point just behind, lost immediate further interest at this stage and retired. Green shortly afterwards began to feel the strain of the fast start and Cooper who had used good judgement gradually reduced the lead and at the Windmill, some 2 miles from home, passed him to go on and win by over 3 minutes, recording his fastest time in this race. Cooper's win was well deserved and popular and his Championship medal is not out of turn. Rathbone fell away in the latter stages and let up Manning into third place. items.label: June 1927
items.sum: Report and results of the club's first track meeting of 1927 at Battersea Park on April 30th, where club members won all three open handicaps (G. R. Maryon the 110 and 300 yards, E. A. Duffett the 880), with club events and the walk won by B. Knifton.
items.s: TRACK SPRING MEETING Report and results of the club's first track meeting of 1927 at Battersea Park on April 30th, where club members won all three open handicaps (G. R. Maryon the 110 and 300 yards, E. A. Duffett the 880), with club events and the walk won by B. Knifton. Our first track meeting on April 30th, at Battersea Park was in all respects a success. Even the weather favoured and with the inclusion of 3 open handicaps a good afternoons sport was provided. The "opens" produced 286 entries which, if a little under the number anticipated, proved reasonably satisfactory. The feature of these events was the victory of a Club member in each. G. R Maryon taking both the 100 and 300 yards and our recent acquisition E A. Duffett the 880. The Novice Mile brought out 26 which was quite a pleasing field by comparison with last year when only 2 competed. The Club events did not quite receive the support that could be expected with exception of the Walk which was above the average for the time of the year. W. F Ball the winner of the sprint is quite a promising runner and being young (he can still compete in the under 18 event) should continue to improve. The Club mile also went to a young member, B. C. Button, who displayed good form and in keeping with the promise given in his first Cross Country run at Feltham last year. B. Knifton repeated his success of Boxing Day and scored a ready victory in the Walk in which the scratch man, A L. Fletcher, put up a very fine performance to finish second in fast time. W. Rice ran well to finish second and actually beat A. Clark, the scratch man, down the straight after being caught and passed. Clark registered just under 4 m. 30 sec. for the mile. RESULTS G R. items.sum: Report and details of the first series of inter-club relays with Croydon, Epsom and Mitcham at Battersea on May 11th, in which Belgrave won the 400 yards, 2 mile and 1,200 yards relays and the 1 mile team race to lead with 16 points, plus a club 2 mile walk won by A. Martin.
items.s: INTER-CLUB RELAYS. Report and details of the first series of inter-club relays with Croydon, Epsom and Mitcham at Battersea on May 11th, in which Belgrave won the 400 yards, 2 mile and 1,200 yards relays and the 1 mile team race to lead with 16 points, plus a club 2 mile walk won by A. Martin. The first series of Inter-Club relays with Croydon, Epsom and Mitcham were decided at Battersea on May 11th, with a Club 2 Mile Walk to open the proceedings. This produced a field of 13 of whom A. Martin, a veteran, eventually won from A L Fletcher who continues to improve and appears likely to shake up the Champions in the near future. J. B Carne made a great effort to hold on when caught but could not maintain the pace and eventually finished 3rd after appearing likely to be beaten on the post by O. Horwood. The first relay event, the 400 yards, looked bad for us in the first stages but eventually we ran out winners by some 2 yards. The 2 Mile was always "good" after J Harris had set up a long lead in the first stage and H. W. Smith had doubled in the next. The 4—300's produced the closest contest of the evening but again we prevailed by a narrow margin with a big tussle for second place between Croydon and Mitcham. The innovation of deciding the hitherto 4 Mile Relay as a 1 mile team race certainly provided a more interesting contest Running 4 from each club and counting and scoring 3, we had a fourth win with A. Clark, W. Rice and H. E. Footer finishing 1st, 2nd and 4th whilst our fourth man F. L Buckingham was close up and actually 6th. So with a maximum score of 16 points we hold a fair lead in the contest from Mitcham with 11, Croydon 8 and Epsom 5. DETAILS 1 A Martin 540 yds. 2 A L Fletcher scr 3 J. B Carne 105 yds 4 O. items.s: THE NATIONAL. Report on the National road walking championship at St Albans, where Belgrave lost the team shield and title to Surrey A.C., with T. W. Green 4th and first club member home, and the Belgrave finishers' times. Our long cherished posession, the Shield and title of National Road Walking Champions, has departed. St Albans, the venue of this years race, will not easily be forgotten by many of our walkers and supporters, for a more disappointing performance could scarcely have been conceived by even the most dismal critic. Really the form on the whole was too bad to be true and as such need not be too seriously considered. Turning to the redeeming features of the race, T. W. Green put up a good show on his first appearance and eventually finished 4th, whilst H. F. King also at a maiden attempt did quite well to finish 7th, So, with a repetition of this form and with E G Cooper and F Rickard at their best we need not fear but that next year we shall be fighting back to regain the lost. This years victors, Surrey A.C., have been "knocking at the door" for some years and certainly their victory was well won. The Cup, donated by Mr. W L. Bayliss for the first Club member to finish, was presented after the race by our President to T. W. Green. The times of those who finished are appended. Act. Pos Time H M S 4 T. W Green 2 59 44 7 H. items.label: June 1927
items.sum: The Hon. Secretary's club notes: the club's growing strength, J. A. Ford's success at the Public Schools Meeting, Dunckley's enforced rest, news of members, the Brighton relay bus trip, the all-night stroll to Brighton on June 18th, dressing-room gossip and a reminder about overdue subscriptions.
items.s: CLUB NOTES. The Hon. Secretary's club notes: the club's growing strength, J. A. Ford's success at the Public Schools Meeting, Dunckley's enforced rest, news of members, the Brighton relay bus trip, the all-night stroll to Brighton on June 18th, dressing-room gossip and a reminder about overdue subscriptions. It is with some amount of pride that I write these club notes, firstly because we are slowly but surely gaining strength, secondly that the class of member now joining is above the average of club novice and thirdly the club officers are always willing to take on any duty that they are asked to undertake. That is the making of a happy club. Our promising member J. A Ford was congratulated at the Public Schools Meeting on his runaway. I hope all the nice things said about him will come true but 1932 is a long time to look forward to. Members will be sorry to hear that Dunckley has been ordered 12 months rest by his medical adviser We thought that we had an Olympic Champion in him and before 1932 We must hope that the enforced rest will not have any ill effect on him but that he will return to the track stronger in health and strength. I am asked to put in my notes that Charles Cook does not want to buy a dog. Several members have received letters from our old friend Speechley. He is going along merrily but misses his walk. If he had been at St Albans we should have heard something from him, as the feeding on the road was of the vegetarian order and Charles always wants a cut from the joint and 2 Veg. Congratulations to our latest benedict, J. G. Flatt. You must not give up running Jimmy, stick to the club and help us win some more championships. I hope my Editor has rubbed it in about our sorry show in the Brighton relay race somewhere else in this issue Still we enjoyed ourselves and the break-down of the bus coming back gave Bayliss a chance to show off his thumping of the domino box. Some of the boys showed signs of possessing quite melodious voices. On Saturday night June 18th the all night stroll will be held if sufficient number of members hand in their names. I should appreciate it if those intending to stroll down (who said and back) will notify me at once so that I can arrange for supper and breakfast. Last year we had a great time so those wishing to see the Brighton road under the glory of a bright full moon please hurry up and put your names down. Well done Stanley. That Colchester race was a great effort. I hear that our Territorial champion has been offered a commission in the Boy Scouts. Over heard in the dressing room :— That Pepper nearly got the bird at our meeting on April 30th. That Harris did get it. That Maryon's mark quite annoyed a well known sports writer. That the Handicappers again got it in the neck. That a certain club member has been asked to represent England at the Bridge on Whit Monday That K O.B wants a gold watch. Good luck to him. That the air round the dust hole is (NOT) full of oxygen. That our Walking Hon. Sec has developed into a real gun man. Members are reminded that it will greatly assist the Hon. Treasurer if they will pay up their subscriptions which are now long overdue. J. A. Ford J. A Ford promising member, congratulated at the Public Schools Meeting on his runaway J. items.s: A FOREWORD. Editor's foreword announcing that The Belgravian is moving from a quarterly to a monthly publication. Our magazine should be a complete record of the Club's undertakings, and a chronicle of the attainments of its individual members. All will agree that these activities are too many to be covered by a quarterly issue of the "Belgravian," therefore we present the first number of a monthly publication. Hereafter no walker need miss a club project because it concerns the runners. No follower need feel "out of it" because of his inability to attend a race. The "Belgravian" shall tell them all about the runners and all about the race. Your support will ensure a "live" Gazette, and a real expression of the Club's opinion and outlook. B.J.T.K. B.J.T.K. items.label: October 1927
items.sum: Tribute to the club's late President, "Bob", recalling how he kept the club going, founded the walking section at Erith, his athletic successes and his work as team manager and handicapper.
items.s: OUR LATE PRESIDENT. Tribute to the club's late President, "Bob", recalling how he kept the club going, founded the walking section at Erith, his athletic successes and his work as team manager and handicapper. Presidents and members come and go, as years roll on, but the Club will never have the member who could put more heart and soul into the welfare of the Belgrave Harriers, than did our late President. The Club has not always been in the prosperous position that it is to-day. Not many years ago a small room in Floor Street, Chelsea, was the meeting place of four members who at that time represented the active section of the Harriers. Bob had little support to encourage him, but he stuck to his job rather than take the easy course of joining another Club. For three years he held the one mile walking championship of the London County Council. His active interest in walking was stimulated by this success, and in the latter part of his career, he decided to render his unflagging services to that branch of sport. An opportunity came to him when during the war, on his transfer from Peterborough to Erith, he formed a Walking Section at the latter place. His typical enterprise was well rewarded, for this nucleus developed into our present very strong walking section. As an athlete his first success of any importance was a 440 yards Handicap at the Oval, which he won in very fast time On another occasion he captured both the 100 yards and 300 yards Handicaps at Southend on the day of the annual Regatta Sports. His many prizes suggest that our favourite was a fast man over distances from 100 to 880 yards So too at walking, for he once had a "bag" of 30 prizes and medals in a single season. During the winter he once took up Boxing, and proved that he was a good allrounder by adding 1st prize in an open competition at Latchmere Baths to his athletic record. As a team manager he was magnificent. Without his zeal and untiring efforts in getting our team together, we should not have won the National Road Walking Championship. During the past four years he was an official Handicapper, appointed by the A.A.A. and R.W.A. In this capacity he concentrated on Walking Handicaps, and during the winter season made all handicaps free of any charge, travelling to Denmark Hill almost every week, in connection with the work. These, my friends, are a few reminiscences of our great friend, and it is up to us all to continue the goodwill and fellowship, and carry on the good work so ably founded and fostered by our late President. W.J.P. W.J.P. W.J.P. National Road Walking Championship London County Council Championships Floor Street, Chelsea Peterborough Erith the Oval Southend Latchmere Baths Denmark Hill A.A.A. R.W.A.

items.label: October 1927
items.sum: Report of the club's Annual General Meeting at Pepy's House on 27 September 1927, covering the officers' reports, rule changes, the election of Mr. Hare as President and the presentation of Brighton Walk mementos.
items.s: THE ANNUAL GENERAL MEETING. Report of the club's Annual General Meeting at Pepy's House on 27 September 1927, covering the officers' reports, rule changes, the election of Mr. Hare as President and the presentation of Brighton Walk mementos. At Pepy's House, on September 27th, we held a conference of great importance to the welfare of the Club Our Chairman voiced the regret of us all at the loss of our President and we stood for a while in reverent silence Business commenced with the report of the Hon. Secretary, who indicated that in spite of lack of success in some undertakings, the Club had a big balance of achievement on the right side. The Hon. Treasurer went through his Balance Sheet with us. It shows a judicious expenditure for 1926-27, and reflects credit on the Chancellors of our Exchequer. Three Proposed Amendments to Rules were carried. They were (1) to limit the number of Vice-Presidents to 16, so that they might not as a body on the Committee out-vote interests equally important as theirs, (2) to permit section-Captains as the representatives of active athletes, to be Committee members, (3) to limit the number of new life-members to 2 per year, and so secure that the honour is conferred only on those who have earned it. The meeting was quick to see the advantages of these alterations, and they were carried without undue delay after a discussion that was short and to the point. Now came the first legitimate opportunity since the last Annual General Meeting, of expressing our appreciations and dissatisfactions. Mr. Hare was unanimously elected President. He has shown us service as Secretary and as Handicapper. Always, he has been the servant of the Club and with our hearty support he shall prove a worthy leader. Fifteen of our Vice-Presidents were re-elected to office. A new Vice-President is Mrs. R. W. Ricketts, who has rendered services to the Club over a long period. Mr. Thomson resigned. During the past year he has put in some very hard work for the Club. We thank him, and are confident that on the Committee his experience will still be at our disposal. In such few words as these must our toilers be dismissed. Their reward must be in the satisfaction which service brings. The new Secretary is a wise choice; we have the right man, whilst his assistant, H. Parker, who as running Hon. Sec. has taken on a job to which nobody could do better justice, is a whole-hearted worker. Our heroes of the Brighton Walk received their mementos amid the deafening plaudits of the Club. After an interval for refreshments, some very bright suggestions were made, and recommended to the Committee for consideration Further remarks are invited on the subject of a series of winter Whist Drives, which seemed to find favour with many. The meeting dispersed at a late hour, with everyone sharing the pleasant impression that concord and fellowship were very much abroad. B.J.T.K. items.label: October 1927
items.sum: Review of the club's 1926-27 season: the Surrey cross country title retained, county colours, the open and evening meetings, the Inter-Club shield won, and the walkers' season including A. L. Fletcher's Inter-Counties walk win and victory in the Brighton Race.
items.s: A REVEIW OF SEASON 1926-27. Review of the club's 1926-27 season: the Surrey cross country title retained, county colours, the open and evening meetings, the Inter-Club shield won, and the walkers' season including A. L. Fletcher's Inter-Counties walk win and victory in the Brighton Race. The Cross Country season, from point of view of racing, was fairly successful. The Club retained the Surrey County Championship which was run over the Surbiton country. The race will be decided over the same course in 1928, when it is hoped that we shall for the third time take home the Pickett Cup In other team championship races, our performances were of the usual mediocrity. It is worthy of mention that our members, A. Clark (Warwick), H. E. Footer and K. B. O'Kell (Surrey) gained their County Colours in the Inter-Counties Cross Country Championships, and H. E. Footer is to be congratulated on winning the Territorial Cross Country Championship. Our Brighton relay failure was a disappointment to the Club, but we hope that a greatly strengthened team will enable us to do much better next year. During the summer bad weather on the whole detracted from the success of our meetings, and in the later days the loss of our President was a sad blow. However, we began well with the experiment of holding an open meeting without the help of a "gate." Fine weather and a good entry of nearly 300 contributed to a success which demands repetition of the meeting. It was gratifying to find the large gathering of supporters and prominent officials from other Clubs congratulating the Belgrave on its enterprise. The summer evening meetings were not supported by members as they should have been. Absentees would do well to take advantage in experience which these gatherings will offer next summer. Despite the drenching rain, the match with the Ashcombe A.C. and Thames V.H. gave us a good evening's sport as well as a good win Cooper Clark won an exciting race in the 440 yards match, and on his further successful performance in the Club Championship we have a worthy successor to our past Club champions. The Inter-Club contests with the Croydon H., Epsom H. and Mitcham A.C. were held after two attempts had been made to hold a meeting at Mitcham. Both were abandoned through bad weather and the result of three meetings instead of four proved us the shield winners for the third time. A feature of the Summer Season was the number of members gaining County Colours We have a bright outlook for next summer with A. Clark, J. Cooper Clark, E. A. Duffett, W. Rice, M. Odell, G. R. Maryon, F. L. G. Buckingham and perhaps K. B. O'Kell to take the Club colours to the fore. Bright spots and black patches, brilliant individual performances but poor team work, characterised the activities of the walkers. The winter season started well, H. F. King, T. W. Green and B. J. T. Knifton showing up prominently in the open handicaps. Full of hope, we went to Sheffield for the Junior. The locals had something to think about when Green and Fletcher came round the last corner side by side in faultless style. The race was a great one to watch, our first pair going away from the field of over 200, and deserving all the good things said about them at the finish. We were not strong enough to capture the team championship, but the Sheffielders were worthy winners. The Senior was not a happy event for us. Green's good performance (4th) stood out once again. It is expresse generally that our team must mean business next year. Get together and train together as far as possible. But that is for next year. We had an interest in the A.A.A. two miles Walk Championship, when our hope A. L. Fletcher finished second to that fine walker, A. G. Pope, after a great struggle in the last lap. We still thought our man could beat Pope, and our confidence was justified at the Inter-Counties meeting. This race was over 3 miles in persistent rain, and Fletcher feeling quite fit and well, went away on the last lap to win by about 25 yards. He gained and richly deserved the greatest applause of the whole meeting. The public are good judges of walking. The climax of the season came with our glorious win in the Surrey Club's Brighton Race. A well-earned vote of thanks has been passed to all those officials and friends who have given their time and energy in helping towards the success of the club meetings. To all—foster the team spirit. It is team work that keeps the Club together and wins its laurels. 1927-28 is a year of great hopes. Let us give our President the opportunity of congratulating the Club on its further successes when he addresses us from the Chair in September next. F.G.T. A. Clark A. items.label: October 1927
items.sum: Report of the Surrey Walking Club's London to Brighton walk, held in heavy rain, in which Green finished 2nd and Belgrave (Green, Rathbone, Manning) won the team race by a point from S.W.C.
items.s: THE S.W C. LONDON-BRIGHTON WALK. Report of the Surrey Walking Club's London to Brighton walk, held in heavy rain, in which Green finished 2nd and Belgrave (Green, Rathbone, Manning) won the team race by a point from S.W.C. A worse day for the walk we have never seen. "Depressions" rather than "impressions" ought to express our recollections. A large crowd watched the start in a heavy downpour. After a brisk half-mile Giani was in the first dozen. Manning led our men with Green and Rathbone walking very easily in the middle of the field and our 4 others following. A crowd of rain-drenched cyclists waiting at Streatham were surprised to see the leaders so soon, and the hot pace caused our critics to think they could not last. Fast times were returned at this point, our men keeping their order, but coming nearer the front of the field. Green, on his first attempt, did not exert himself until beyond Croydon, and then a fast, steady pace took him ahead of Manning and Horton (S.W.C.) who were almost side by side. Evidently the weather overcame the stout courage of the latter, for he retired soon after. The beating of wind and rain against the walkers made havoc, especially among the lean ones. Booker (S.W.C.) and several others were missed at this time through cold. At Merstham, Green had walked up to 11th place, and at Redhill the judges, in the Post Office out of the pelting rain, recorded him 6th Horley saw him 3rd, with Holt (2nd) nearly seven minutes ahead and Giani (1st) still another 7 minutes in front. Not until after reaching Hand Cross did Green overtake Holt, but at Albourne he had left the latter 9 minutes behind! Giani's fast work early on had, however, made his victory secure, and Green, walking quite as fast now as the winner, finished 2nd, eleven minutes behind. Well walked both! The excitement of the team race must have produced heart-failure among weaker men. Rathbone hot on the track of Manning passed him at Merstham. At Crawley our hopes and doubts made us feverish. S.W.C. lead us by one point! Rathbone came to the rescue, walking into 7th place and reversing the score, while Manning, in difficulty for the first time, held on grimly. At Dale Hill, Green (2nd), Rathbone (now 6th) and Manning (12th), still lead by a point from S.W.C., and finished in these positions, much to the relief and delight of Belgravians. Our members, Waltam, Laurie and Thomas walked well, beating 10½ hours, whilst Winner who found the slippery road difficult was inside 11 hours. What a day! Continuous rain soaked us for seven hours; food and equipment all clammy and everything wet. After Bolney the sun shone, and we, poor playthings of the weather, began to Steam. Still our enthusiasm, like the weather, was unrestrained. After hot sea water baths in Brills we felt O.K. Then came the mending of broken feet and filling of empty stomachs. On reflection, and considering that we won the team race, it was for us a delightful day. H.P. items.label: October 1927
items.sum: Report and results of the club's opening 5 miles walking handicap, won by A. Martin, and 3 miles running handicap, won by A. E. Smith.
items.s: OPENING RUN AND WALK. Report and results of the club's opening 5 miles walking handicap, won by A. Martin, and 3 miles running handicap, won by A. E. Smith. McMullen and Knifton caught S. L. King at about 1½ miles and in the next mile they passed in turn Briggs, Tilley, Hawkes and S. S. Fletcher. MacMullen who had been delayed 60 yards through enforced attention to his shorts began to feel the effect of his effort and dropped away. Fish, walking strongly was the next ahead of Knifton who did not overtake him until the four miles point had been reached. By this time it was clear that the long markers would score. Peacock was expected to be well up, but he appeared (like most of us) tired towards the finish. As he was fairly fit his effort of a week before in the "twenty" was perhaps responsible for this. Martin was fighting fit and won comfortably. Elson, a new member, made good use of his start to finish fifth. A. E. Smith ran steadily past the opposition in the 3 miles handicap. At 2 miles he was second to G. Tyrer, a veteran with 4 minutes start, whom he caught at 2½ miles Hereafter he ran unchallenged to win by 25 yards. The time of the winner and Duffett, was equalled by Buckingham in October, 1925, and has been beaten only by A. E. Elliott (S.A.C.), who accomplished 15 minutes 9 seconds in November, 1924. Pyers effort of 15 minutes 15 seconds in 1923 was another good performance. Results show that the number of speed men in the Club has increased since 1925. In that year, only two men could beat 16 minutes when this annual fixture was held, whereas this time five accomplished the feat. Start. Handicap. Nett. 1. A. Martin 7.20 40.57 48.17 2. V. J. items.label: October 1927
items.h: INTER-CLUB C.C. RACE WITH ASHCOMBE A.C. AND THAMES VALLEY H.
items.sum: Report of the first inter-club cross-country race with Ashcombe A.C. and Thames Valley H., won by Duffett with Belgrave taking the team race, and the result of the members' 5 miles sealed handicap run with it.
items.s: INTER-CLUB C.C. RACE WITH ASHCOMBE A.C. AND THAMES VALLEY H. Report of the first inter-club cross-country race with Ashcombe A.C. and Thames Valley H., won by Duffett with Belgrave taking the team race, and the result of the members' 5 miles sealed handicap run with it. The first race of the series took place from our Headquarters on Saturday, October 22nd There was not the number of absentees one might have expected; we are getting used to the rain. A field of 74 (comprising—"Ashes" 20, "Valley" 23 and Bels." 31), faced our President for the start. The course was the usual "5," starting at the top of Lanviston Road, across the golf links, past Cæsers Well to the Horse Ride and then eft across Beverley Brook to the Robin Hood Gate. Up, and round Spankers Hill to return over the same course. Little need be said of the actual race, as Duffett, always up with the leaders, came away when he liked, to win by 20 seconds. The team race was always ours, and scoring 12 aside, our team finished in the first 20 places scoring 127 points against 282 by the Valley and 340 by Ashcombe Several of our "Juniors" ran well, including Button, Tom Pritchard, Davis, Field and others. A new member, Robertshaw, is promising and will do much better. We were pleased to see Button with us as he will soon be off to Australia. We wish him luck The sealed handicap for members represents Arthur Clark, who had gone home for the week-end. at scratch. It was pleasing to see Bayliss amongst the prizes; quite a long time has passed since he was mentioned. Our Secretary is a good team man, and generally sacrifices his own chances in helping and encouraging others along. 5 Miles' Sealed Handicap, held in conjunction with Inter-Team Race. items.label: October 1927
items.sum: Walking notes on the Brighton Walk, the first road handicap won by A Martin, the club's Open walk on 26 November and the 7 mile handicap for the O. Horwood Cup.
items.s: WITH THE WALKERS. Walking notes on the Brighton Walk, the first road handicap won by A Martin, the club's Open walk on 26 November and the 7 mile handicap for the O. Horwood Cup. Since our last issue, the most outstanding performance was that of our long distance men in the Surrey W. C.'s Brighton Walk, last September. We hope that T. W Green with the experience of this race will win the "Victory" Cup next year. Thanks are due to the attendants, who had a very trying time. The first road handicap on 8th October brought twenty-two entries, of which sixteen started, and although racing fitness was not general, only two failed to finish. A Martin was first off and was never headed, while Knifton who returned fastest time could get no nearer than fourth. In our own "Open," we expect the support of all our active walkers, and hope to be well supported as usual by other clubs, on November 26th. The Club will support as many Open Races as possible, and all wishing to be entered in teams should send their entry form and fee to the Walking Secretary, so that he receives them not later than the Saturday preceding the day of the race. All Juniors should note that the 7 Mile Handicap for the O. Horwood Cup with handicap race is down for decision on December 17th. S.L.K T. W. Green T. W Green 2nd in the Surrey W.C. Brighton Walk T. items.label: October 1927
items.sum: Running notes on the coming South of Thames Junior race at Tolworth, the South of Thames Championship, team races and the Surrey County Team Race for juniors.
items.s: RUNNING NOTES. Running notes on the coming South of Thames Junior race at Tolworth, the South of Thames Championship, team races and the Surrey County Team Race for juniors. The first important open team race, is the South of Thames Junior, which will be held on November 19th, at Tolworth, over the S.A.C. 5 Miles course. After winning this event in 1925, we were 7th last year, which is quite good when one remembers that the winning team is barred. Practically the whole of last year's first team are again available, and there will be one or two additions. We shall enter as many teams as possible. The South of Thames Championship will be held on February 11th, at a venue to be fixed. Members are particularly asked to support all the friendly team races and socials, especially the away fixtures. Where these events may be some distance from Headquarters, every endeavour will be made to obtain cheap travelling facilities. In the team races, it should be remembered that members who are not good enough to score in big events are enabled to count by, as far as possible, an "all-to-score" arrangement. The special attention of all "Junior" runners is called to the Surrey County Team Race on December 3rd. This fixture is for juniors in age, being confined to runners under the age of 18 years on day of race, and is over 3 miles. We won this event in 1924, and our turn is about due again. Will all members eligible and who are qualified, advise the Running Hon. Secretary? H.P. H.P. H.P. South of Thames Junior South of Thames Championship Surrey County Team Race Tolworth S.A.C.

items.label: October 1927
items.sum: The Hon. Secretary's notes on the start of the season, new members, the club's Open Walk, newspaper notices, subscriptions and the R. W. Ricketts fund.
items.s: HON. SECRETARY'S NOTES. The Hon. Secretary's notes on the start of the season, new members, the club's Open Walk, newspaper notices, subscriptions and the R. W. Ricketts fund. The Cross Country and Road Walking season has commenced in a most hearty fashion. The first two races were well supported, and there are bright prospects for a successful season for both sections. It is pleasing to note the number of new members one now sees, especially amongst the Runners; I would warn them against racing in training. Our Open Walk is being held as usual, and there are rumours of a huge entry. Let us hope our Walking Secretary, S. L. King, will beat the record at his first venture. All Club Notices will be printed in the "Illustrated Sport and Kennel" (every Friday), and the "South London Press" (on Tuesdays). The attention given us by these journals is worthy of your support. Club Subscriptions for 1927-28 not already paid should be given to Mr. A. E. Masher at once, and members in arrears are invited to send something off their debt. The R. W. Ricketts fund is still open, and continues to progress. W. L. BAYLISS. S. L. King S. L. King Walking Secretary Mr. A. E. Masher Mr. A. E. Masher receives club subscriptions R. W. Ricketts R. W. items.label: November 1927
items.sum: The new President, W. H. Hare, thanks members for his election, pays tribute to his late predecessor and appeals for team work and goodwill in the Club.
items.s: BY OUR PRESIDENT. The new President, W. H. Hare, thanks members for his election, pays tribute to his late predecessor and appeals for team work and goodwill in the Club. I welcome this opportunity afforded me by "The Belgravian" to express to all members my thanks and appreciation for the honour conferred on me by my election as President of the Belgrave Harriers It is now my greatest hope that I may be enabled to justify the confidence placed in me, and that my period of office shall be one of great progress in the welfare of the Club I must confess that I have at times hoped that I might in some distant year be considered worthy of election to this office, but any happy thought on the early attainment of an ideal is now saddened by the circumstances that hastened the achievement The wonderful personality of our late President will, however, set an example to me, and all those that knew him, and memory of his staunch and whole-hearted efforts for the Club, will supply all the inspiration needed to carry on his good work. This is a duty that we may all endeavour to carry out. It is apparent at the present time, that a spirit of goodwill, hope, and confidence in the future, is amongst all our members, which is to me most encouraging and satisfactory Doubtless team work of the Executive and team work in competition is the secret of success, and if this is maintained, I have little doubt that we shall continue to prosper in every way. If I may express a few words on this occasion to any member that may not share the views of the Committee, I would say, "Take an active interest in the activities of the Club, not however as a destructive critic; pass your ideas in the right way to the right quarter (the Hon Secretary likes a big post); consider the other man's point of view as well as your own, be assured that the Committee desire the good of the greater number, and have patience with a genuine error or misunderstanding." To all I would say "Remember that the Club is, and is judged, as you make it and by your example let the Belgrave Harriers be 'Second to none.'" This is my greatest wish and with your help and co-operation I look forward with every confidence to the future for the fruition of our great hopes and ambitions. W. H. HARE. W. H. Hare W. H. HARE President; newly elected

items.label: November 1927
items.sum: Club notes: news of Ken O'Kell in Staffordshire, George Powell's marriage, Belgraves at the Centurions' dinner, Will Brown's news of Harry's bereavement in Australia, and a list of new members.
items.s: CLUB NOTES. Club notes: news of Ken O'Kell in Staffordshire, George Powell's marriage, Belgraves at the Centurions' dinner, Will Brown's news of Harry's bereavement in Australia, and a list of new members. A recent letter from our old friend "Ken" O'Kell shows him doing his best to keep fit. Although not with us personally, he is with us in spirit. He says he has had an occasional spin with the North Staffordshire Harriers, but is unable to train seriously owing to having to work Saturday afternoons and Sunday mornings He sends his Xmas Greetings in advance and hopes to dispense them himself in the Park on Boxing Day. Apparently he is making headway in his new sphere, and I am sure you will all wish him success. George Powell, the Club's strong man in field events, is to be congratulated on his marriage, and we wish him happiness. Members requiring information on the subject (field events, not marriage) will do well to receive the advice he is glad to give. At the Annual Dinner of the Centurions held on November 25th, the Belgraves were well represented. Three of their badged and certified insanes, J B. Belchamber, J. K. Chalk and J. N. Thomas were present, whilst the 4th, G. Tompkins, sent a letter excusing his absence. Will Brown, the record-holder and a brother of one of our former Presidents, was present; and from him it was learned that Harry, who has been in Australia for the past six years, has had the misfortune to lose a daughter—quite a child—by meningitis. Our old members all know what a good friend of the Club Harry was. They remember him affectionately, and when sympathising with him in his bereavement they will deeply regret that they were unable, through distance and lack of knowledge, to express by some token that the old bonds still hold. The following have lately joined us; may this be not the last time they will come into the limelight. L. J. Mann, F. Forster, A. E. Betts, J. C. McLean, A. J. Lander, A Robertshaw, J. T. Fletcher, R. G. Hillier, W. W. S. Mitchell, S Tranmer and J. A. Hill. items.sum: Report and result of the friendly seven-mile team walk against the Metropolitan Police A.A. at Wimbledon on 12 November, won by S. A. Holland of the Police, with Belgrave winning the team race 96 points to 114.
items.s: WALK WITH METROPOLITAN POLICE A.A. Report and result of the friendly seven-mile team walk against the Metropolitan Police A.A. at Wimbledon on 12 November, won by S. A. Holland of the Police, with Belgrave winning the team race 96 points to 114. On 12th November, for the second year in succession, this friendly team contest was held over our seven-mile course at Wimbledon. So strong were both teams that all concerned must have been sensible of the compliment paid to their respective clubs by the furnishing of so thoroughly representative an opposition. (And here a word of praise may well be given to our new Walking Secretary His duties as party whip are being carried out in a most efficient manner, and rarely have our walkers answered parade call so abundantly and consistently as they are doing this season Like Father O'Flynn in the ballad he has evidently "a wonderful way wid him"). A keen and enjoyable race for both individual placings and team honours was the natural outcome. The field of 33 went away very fast led during the first mile by H. F. King. Hereabouts he was joined by Tommy Green, S. A. Holland, A. L. Fletcher and W. Batson. At four miles the five were still together, with the Belgraves just leading on points in the team race In the last lap A. L. Fletcher, who had only just resumed training after a well-deserved rest, dropped back early on, but the four others held together for the greater part of the lap; S. A Holland eventually winning by three yards from T. W. Green. Only about 100 yards separated the 1st and 4th men at the finish. The team race was decided on the University system of scoring, ten a side counting, and was won by our boys with 96 points against 114. Details : Bel.: 2, 4, 5, 6, 8, 10, 13, 15, 16, 17—96. items.label: November 1927
items.sum: Report and result of the 5-mile inter-club cross-country contest against Thames Valley Harriers and Ashcombe A.C. at Roehampton on 12 November, won by Belgrave (69 points) with E. A. Duffett first home.
e: Inter Club Contest v. Thames Valley Harriers and Ashcombe A.C.
items.s: INTER CLUB CONTEST Report and result of the 5-mile inter-club cross-country contest against Thames Valley Harriers and Ashcombe A.C. at Roehampton on 12 November, won by Belgrave (69 points) with E. A. Duffett first home. Against Thames Valley Harriers and Ashcombe Athletic Club It was under wretched weather conditions that on November 12th, we turned out for our usual popular fixture over the Ashcombe's course at Roehampton. Nevertheless a very good muster started and no less than 62 finished the course, which was a circular one of 5 miles, the going on the whole being fairly arduous. Owing to the now very dangerous crossing into Richmond Park at the Robin Hood gate, our hosts had very wisely altered their course. Instead of turning right when reaching the "Beverley," the field turned left, and went over the famous "Toast Rack" and "Dismal Swamp" area. At the start Belgrave were well to the fore, Duffett taking the lead, followed by Footer, Pyer and Tame. Soon after came Khlopin, Smith, Rice and Pritchard These positions were maintained practically throughout the race, and excellent packing enabled us to win quite comfortably Webb put up a very creditable performance, but could not quite get up to the leaders. W. Pritchard is to be congratulated on his excellent running and one of our new men, Robertshaw, shewed up very promisingly. items.label: November 1927
items.sum: Report and result of the South of Thames junior cross-country race at Tolworth on 19 November, won by A. W. V. Tebbutt of St. George's Services S.C., with P. Khlopin first Belgrave man in 5th and the Belgrave "A" team 3rd.
e: South of Thames Junior Cross Country Championship
items.s: SOUTH OF THAMES "JUNIOR" C.C. RACE. Report and result of the South of Thames junior cross-country race at Tolworth on 19 November, won by A. W. V. Tebbutt of St. George's Services S.C., with P. Khlopin first Belgrave man in 5th and the Belgrave "A" team 3rd. This race was held at Tolworth, on Saturday, 19th November, from The United Services Club, the headquarters of the Surrey A C. The weather conditions were not of the best, rain falling throughout the afternoon, while the course was on the heavy side 107 runners, representing 14 teams, faced the starter who got them away very poorly, resulting in our "A" team getting "left at the post." They soon began, however, to work their way to the front, and coming out of the starting field Khlopin was lying 7th, with several other members of the team in close attendance. After the first circuit of the country, the above-named was still first of our men, with Robertshaw just behind. As the latter was in the "B" team this was not too promising, for St. George's and Surrey were packing fairly well Out into the country again the field streamed, by this time well strung out, and with several looking the worse for wear. When they came into sight once more, Khlopin was 5th, and although making a fine effort to overhaul the men in front was unable to improve on his position at the finish. Our next man was Wally Bayliss, who had run a splendid race, then came Rice (a disappointment this, as he was expected to do much better), Buckingham completed our scoring four, who are to be congratulated on finishing 3rd in the team race, a fair performance. Our runners, we feel sure, will do much better in the later races of the season. Among the individuals, Robertshaw was the outstanding man, as he could have finished very close to the leaders, but sacrificed his place in order to help the "A" team men along. W. D. Pritchard unfortunately fell when near home, and sustaining an injury to his ankle, had to hobble in. This accounted for his lowly position A word of praise to the officials of the Club, and also some of the senior members who went out into the rain and slush to do their best to assist the team, by instructions as to how they were placed, etc., a procedure which is very helpful and which has assisted the Club to win races in the past. One other pleasing feature was the fact that of the 25 Belgrave runners in the race, all completed the course, and some of the novices are to be commended for the pluck they showed in sticking it, especially as they have not so much depending on them as the "A" team men. They showed the fine spirit which is constantly being revealed in cross-country running Result :— 1 St. George's Services S.C, 1, 7, 10, 12—30 3 Belgrave "A," 5, 9, 16, 22—52 9 " "B" 23, 57, 62, 67—209 13. items.s: CLUB OPEN WALK. Report of the Club's open walk, won again by T. W. Green, with the Belgrave "A" team winning the scratch team race and the "B" team the handicap; F. Elson's handicap time is printed as 58 2 in the results but 55-2 in the team handicap, and V J Peacock's as 54.33 and 54-23. Such a fine race as it was the lot of our Club to promote is seldom seen Yet again T W Green, "our star artist of fair walking" (F G T ) wore down his opponents and accomplished a performance second only to that of Goodwin who in 1924 won in 54m 9s At a mile the field of 154, including 21 teams, was stretched out over nearly 300 yards, and a round dozen were spread over the width of the road disputing the lead. McMullen, Hyde, Pope, Scammel, Green, Fletcher and Holland, were the most prominent. The race proceeded with the first position undecided and not until two miles from home could Green, Pope and Hyde shake off the others. We congratulate Pope and Hyde on their very fine walking Our "A" team packed in fine fashion to win the scratch team race. The "B" team were well up and in addition got home in the handicap This team work was one of the finest features of the race The style of our men was good and they walked well within themselves. Saunders was nearest in the handicap (5th) and his steady progress will soon bring additional honours to the Club. Although McMullen finished 13th, this was not good enough to score for the "A" team However, when he received his award as first Belgrave man home not to take another prize, a hearty round of applause, unmistakable in its sincerity, must have compensated him A. items.label: November 1927
items.sum: Notes on Belgrave juniors in the Surrey county youths' cross-country race at Rose Hill, where Coleman finished 16th and Clapham 35th, with a note on Oscar Horwood being struck by a golf-ball in the club "open".
e: South of Thames Junior Cross Country
items.s: SURREY YOUTH'S RACE. Notes on Belgrave juniors in the Surrey county youths' cross-country race at Rose Hill, where Coleman finished 16th and Clapham 35th, with a note on Oscar Horwood being struck by a golf-ball in the club "open". I hope that our Juniors who went to Rose Hill for the County Juniors race will not be too disappointed at their failure—if it was a failure For after all was it their fault? The "Senior Juniors" also failed to live up to expectations in the South of Thames race, and for the same reason. The training our runners get is not severe enough for cross-country purposes The course selected by the Mitcham A C. was certainly severe for runners under 18 years of age to race over, particularly for those who have not trained over the heavy stuff—so I think they are to be commiserated with. Our two members who did finish ran very well indeed. At the end of the first circuit Coleman was 20th, and Clapham 37th but both improved on the second lap and Coleman finished 16th and Clapham 35th. Both are to be congratulated as I believe it is their first race over country And I hope our other two members who started will not be discouraged The father of one was telling me he was a member of the now defunct Battersea Harriers, and was an original member of the "Bels " So let us hope he will give his son some good advice and carry on the good work. Oscar Horwood had a very painful experience in our "open," but he has fully recovered now When crossing the golf-links on the last lap he was struck amid-ships by a golf-ball. We feel very indignant about the matter but it must be passed over as an unfortunate accident. H P. Coleman Coleman 20th after first circuit, finished 16th in the County Juniors race Clapham Clapham 37th after first circuit, finished 35th in the County Juniors race Oscar Horwood Oscar Horwood struck by a golf-ball on the last lap in "our open"; fully recovered H. items.label: November 1927
items.sum: Humorous piece by a member ordered by the Editor to write notes for the magazine, who settles on praising the club's Sunday morning walks and invites more members to join them.
items.s: THE NEW TERROR. Humorous piece by a member ordered by the Editor to write notes for the magazine, who settles on praising the club's Sunday morning walks and invites more members to join them. Go!" he said, "Write a few notes for the Mag. Anything will do." The command left me dumbfounded. I wondered what crime I had committed that demanded such severe punishment and decided to appeal against the sentence. "I can't—I don't," I stammered wretchedly, biting my lips and forcing my nails into the palms of my hands—but all in vain. The Tyrant fixed me with his eye, his face assumed a greenish, unearthly tinge, his teeth were clenched, his jaw set as if he had walked out of the pages of an Ethel M. Dell novel. "Anything will do," he repeated slowly, softly, relentlessly, and then turned to walk away. I nervously touched him on the shoulder. "But—" I began "And let me have it next Tuesday evening without fail," he said sternly. My heart quavered, a lump formed in my throat, tears came before my eyes and my six-feet-three seemed to shrink to three-feet-six. I sat down mournfully to consider the monstrous injustice of it all, this appalling sorrow that had come into my blameless life. As I tried to write something that would be emotional, poignant, inspiring, tragic, entertaining, elevating, humorous, fresh, vigorous, mirth-provoking, sentimental, apt, topical and original, I thought of our Editor as the reincarnation of an old-time Inquisitor gloating over the discomfiture of his victims Then came the business of choosing a subject I thought of writing on "Handicapping," but decided not to trespass on the field of Edgar Wallace and A Conan Doyle, our foremost mystery writers I then thought of compiling a series of questions after the style of the daily newspapers but could only get as far as No 1. Who was it went past his station on the return from Epsom, and why? A dozen themes suggested themselves only to be rejected one by one until, finally, I decided to write on the delights of Sunday strolling. Firstly, comes the triumph of Mind over Matter—the early rising whilst others still sleep. Then a hearty breakfast and off to the meeting place, arriving punctually at 10 o'clock. The President arrives, a start is made and tongues begin to wag. Mental recreation as well as physical is afforded on these strolls. Subjects of conversation are infinite in their variety and have included, inter alia, an infallible method of backing greyhounds, numerous war experiences, how the totalisator is operated, etc , etc. Perhaps one day we may even learn how a handicap is prepared! Who knows? Less likely things have been known to happen. Did not a certain member win two prizes at one of the evening meetings during the summer? We should like to see more members on the Sunday morning walks. Their company and conversation will be most heartily welcomed. Give these strolls a trial. It will cost you nothing and if you are disatisfied your money will be refunded. I am afraid that this is beginning to read like a patent medicine advertisement, but the fact remains that ALL are welcome, walkers, runners, and those hovering between the two If necessary, I am sure the Committee will arrange for the strollers to leave in packs of fifty at intervals. You will be there next Sunday? Good It is with considerable satisfaction that I find I have written a few notes ("Anything will do"—the voice haunts me still), and so put an end to my trials and troubles Away! sleepless nights and dismal days, for my period of pen nibbling and inspiration-seeking is ended. Despair is banished and Rejoicing enthroned in its stead. The task is finished But (pessimistic thought) there is one cloud on the horizon. After a short while another issue of "The Belgravian" will become due, fresh notes will be required Who will be the next unfortunate compelled by a heartless Editor, to submit "a few notes " Who? You? A.A H. A.A. H. A.A H. initials sign-off A.A H. Ethel M. Dell Ethel M. Dell novelist, mentioned Edgar Wallace Edgar Wallace mystery writer, mentioned A. items.label: November 1927
items.sum: Social notes announcing the club's first dance at Battersea Town Hall on 11 January and social evenings at St. John's Hall, and describing social runs with Epsom (hosted on 29 October) and Highgate Harriers, with a run with St. George's Services A.C. to come on 7 January.
items.s: SOCIAL. Social notes announcing the club's first dance at Battersea Town Hall on 11 January and social evenings at St. John's Hall, and describing social runs with Epsom (hosted on 29 October) and Highgate Harriers, with a run with St. George's Services A.C. to come on 7 January. Our first Dance takes place on Wednesday, 11th January, at Battersea Town Hall (Grand Hall). Members are earnestly requested to give their support on this occasion by bringing their friends, and so help to make the evening a financial as well as a social success. Tickets 1/6 each, may be had on application to Hon. Social Secretary. A few Social evenings have been arranged, to be held on Saturdays, at St. John's Hall, and you are advised to book the following dates for these affairs :— 28th January. 18th February. It is very pleasing to see how well our "away" fixtures are being supported. But even now, looking down the list of members, one finds several names of "distance" men who should be with us on Saturday afternoons, and I feel that these members would find the benefit of a winter training, when racing on the track in the summer On the 29th October, 25 strong, we journeyed to Epsom for a social spin with our old friends in Mitcham, Croydon and Epsom. Epsom as hosts, gave us a run over about 5 miles of good country where plenty of mud and water were found This was quite a new experience to some of our members, but they must remember that it is good training. Far heavier country is often found in big events We seem to have wandered from Epsom; but to continue. After the run we hied ourselves to the "King's Head" where our Epsom friends had provided a repast. Although a large crowd did not stay to the sing-song afterwards, I think I am safe in saying that those who did, enjoyed themselves And those who stayed to the end and heard Jannaway and Bond in their rendering of one or two very old-fashioned songs, and the whistling turn provided by one of our friends from Epsom, will not forget them in a hurry. The following week we were the guests of Highgate H , at Edgware, where again "good country" was run over, and after a good tea a social evening was enjoyed by quite a number who stayed. On January 7th, we shall have better acquaintance with that formidable strength, the St. George's Services A.C., at Wimbledon on a social run. items.sum: Mock answers to correspondents with pen-names, joking about increasing walking speed, getting fat, embrocation and swimming the Channel.
items.s: ANSWERS TO CORRESPONDENTS. Mock answers to correspondents with pen-names, joking about increasing walking speed, getting fat, embrocation and swimming the Channel. "Walker" (Battersea).—Yes, there are several good ways of increasing speed that we can recommend. For instance, by joining the running section, or by borrowing a motor-bike. The most effective method, is undoubtedly by taking longer strides (these should not, however, exceed three yards), and by covering the ground more quickly. "X Y Z." (Chelsea).—See answer to "Felix" below. "Novice" (Liverpool).—If you want to get fat, the best way is to buy it from your butcher like a decent Belgravian. "Ratherboney' (Spain).—The embrocation to which you refer is excellent. It is also good as hair-oil and is useful for polishing boots. Moreover, it makes a refreshing drink, but we wish it would lose its odour. Phew!! "Felix" (Brixton).—See reply to "X Y.Z." above. "Enquirer (S W 14) —Yes, she swam the Channel without a costume Whilst agreeing that this would similarly make for greater freedom of action for cross-country work, we are afraid that objection might possibly be raised in certain quarters. "Alpha" (Hammersmith).—We can trace nothing in the A.A.A. Rules to prevent the use of an umbrella and goloshes for cross-country running during the wet weather. Battersea Chelsea Liverpool Spain Brixton Hammersmith

Green, F Rickard), the Club Junior Championship for the O Horwood Cup on 17 December, the annual 3 miles at Battersea Park and Dagenham H's open handicap on 7 January. A pleasing feature of all races this season, is the number of club walkers competing; 15 turning out in the R W A Open, 25 in the Inter-Club, and 27 in our own Open I hope all walkers will try to improve still more on these numbers, by turning out on all possible occasions. Several of our members have been successful in races outside the Club, E. L. Reeve having won off scratch in a handicap promoted by the Southend and County H , while T W. Green secured fastest loser's prize in the Southern Railway Worthing to Brighton handicap F Rickard was placed 7th in the All England Police 10 mile championship, and was in the winning team. The Club "Junior" Championship (7 miles) for the O Horwood Cup, is to be decided on 17th December, and all those eligible to compete are asked to support this race. We look forward to startling performances from our Godstone enthusiasts who are training with plenty of "pep." While the "men" support the Surrey W.C walk, the "boys" must flock to Battersea Park for our annual 3 miles tussle. Dagenham H are a club of some two years' standing, and it behoves us to enter strong teams in their 7 miles' open handicap venture, on January 7th. It must not be said that we could not stay out the season in the style we began. Send your entries in at an early date to the Walkers' Secretary, S. L. KING, 3 Artillery Row Buildings, S W.1. E. L. items.s: RUNNING. Running notes urging members to the match at Feltham against Thames Valley H and Ashcombe A C, and to the 7 miles C.C. Championship at Wimbledon on 31 December and the Surrey County C C. Championship at Tolworth on 14 January. It is hoped that all members will make an effort to turn up to the match at Feltham on the 17th, versus Thames Valley H and Ashcombe A C. We were 30 starters, not counting three late arrivals at Roehampton in our last match Cheap tickets can be had at the Booking Offices (1/2 Clapham Junction; 9d. Barnes). Will Andrews and Jimmy Flat come along and help to swell the party? Or perhaps Jimmy doesn't like leaving the fireside now that he is a benedict! At any rate the life seems to suit him for he is looking remarkably well But for the sake of the team I hope it won't slow him up Efforts are being made to find a new course at Wimbledon for our 7 miles C.C. Championship on December 31st Our recent trouble in the South of Thames, is one that will recur unless we find more mud and slush for training purposes (Do not let this discourage the faint-hearted. He should know that hot baths are provided afterwards, but even so, beauty specialists advocate mud-baths) Full strength must be whipped up for the Surrey County C C. Championship at Tolworth on January 14th. Let us hope that the S. of T. experience together with the yet undiscovered bogs and swamps of Wimbledon, will provide us the means to win. Enquiries to H. items.label: January 1928
items.sum: Club notes on the missing club mascot, A. E. Jones's return from Canada, Duffett's run against Cambridge University, members' showings in business-house championships, thanks to donors and A. Stone's King's Police Medal for a Thames rescue.
items.s: CLUB NOTES. Club notes on the missing club mascot, A. E. Jones's return from Canada, Duffett's run against Cambridge University, members' showings in business-house championships, thanks to donors and A. Stone's King's Police Medal for a Thames rescue. At our Dinner last year a very enthusiastic but non-actual member presented the Club with a Mascot. Those who journeyed to Reading in February will remember the desperate efforts made by a rival Club to capture it, particularly on the return journey. Can any member give us news of this mascot, or will the present holder bring it forth? We have to welcome back from Canada an old friend— A. E. Jones. Jones gave every promise of developing into a good class runner. We hope to have his services again very shortly. Friend Duffett was the recipient of an invitation to run in a team arranged by Mr Holt, the well known A.A.A. and S L.H. Official, against Cambridge University at Cambridge, on December 3rd. He put up quite a good show over the heavy University course, and finished 8th, being 3rd for his team. Muggridge and Johnstone were 1st and 2nd respectively for Mr. Holt's team. After the race both teams sat down to dinner, and Duffett tells us that he had a very jolly time. Several members have been shewing up in various championships. On the 10th "Business house day," we found B. C Button running in the London Shipping C.C.C., and finishing 2nd. We are glad this youngster did something before he shook the dust of Old England from his feet. Our new member, G. Webb, was in the Civil Service event. When we look at this result and see the names of many prominent runners after his, we say he must have run well. Coming to the Brewers—we have to congratulate Arthur Clark on his win for the second year in succession, and the gratifying result of his efforts to lead in a winning team. W. D. Pritchard and W. Gage were respectively 3rd and 6th in this race. May the New Year be a happy and prosperous one for all club members and the club. We thank Messrs. J. Belchamber and H. Evans for their generous assistance to the gazette funds. Will members please notify the Hon. Secretary of changes of address, so that letters may not be mis-directed. A. STONE one of our walkers and an all-round athlete, has been honoured in the New Year's List by the conferment on him of the Kings Police Medal. Early one morning, a few months back, he dived from Westminster Bridge in the darkness to rescue an unfortunate person from drowning. The circumstances evolved great personal risk to the rescuer. A. items.s: 7 MILES' CLUB JUNIOR ROAD WALKING CHAMPIONSHIP. O. Horwood's report of the club's 7 miles junior road walking championship and handicap, won by Scammell with Saunders taking the handicap, with the full result table. "Gee, it's cold!" was the general opinion before the start of the race, and several remarked that they did not fancy stripping on such a day (the truth is that on these occasions they wish they were not so old), but long before the race was over my sympathy was with the judges, timekeeper and other officials, for it was indeed cold This no doubt led to a very fast start, set up by Scammell, followed by that promising youngster, Elson, who hung on gamely, but once Scammell settled down, he made sure of the result, and added his name to the plinth for the second time There was a very decided improvement on the times which argues well for the Junior championship to come. The walking generally was good, with one exception, and I am sure the excepted member, if he takes the advice given, will with patience obliterate his fault, and overtake his field at a more even pace—not in the quickest possible time. The handicap was always a forgone conclusion for Saunders, who well deserved his win and improves in every race. The same refers to Elson, whose future will be watched with great interest by the club Tilly was again amongst the prizes, but he should make more use of his pace earlier in the race and not hang on to walkers who are too slow for him. There were several non-starters, who would have made the race more interesting, and would have helped to close up the Handicap results. The writer, making a few remarks after the prize-giving, omitted to mention the holder of the Cup, A. L. Fletcher, who forfeited his Junior qualification by his sterling walking on the track. We all wish him the best of luck for the future, and feel sure he will add more laurels to his own and the club's. He will be a great acquisition to the Senior Section. items.h: "STROLL, SUNDAY MORNING NEXT. MEET PUTNEY BRIDGE, SOUTH SIDE, AT 10 A.M."
items.sum: Feature inviting members to the club's Sunday-morning training strolls of 14 to 16 miles, describing a sample route from Putney Bridge through Richmond Park, Bushey Park and Hampton Court and back.
items.s: "STROLL, SUNDAY MORNING NEXT. MEET PUTNEY BRIDGE, SOUTH SIDE, AT 10 A.M." Feature inviting members to the club's Sunday-morning training strolls of 14 to 16 miles, describing a sample route from Putney Bridge through Richmond Park, Bushey Park and Hampton Court and back. Often enough the notice has met your eye, but have you ever acted upon it and gone to the meet? Perhaps there is a doubt as to what transpires. Then let us assist you Originally intended as supplementary training for walkers, the Stroll did at times degenerate into hurried scrambles, but of recent years they have been conducted at a much more sedate pace, and of a distance that is not beyond any of our active members. Strangely enough, the majority of "the regulars" are running members and have included those who are purely short distance track men Since their subsequent running has been improved it proves very definitely the benefit of "Strolling" for "Training" The distance covered is now in the region of 14 to 16 miles, which at first sight appears alarming, but really is not. Try, if you doubt. Let us endeavour to conduct you on a sample stroll. We leave Putney, taking the road by the river, and in 10 minutes are on Barnes Common. Already the town is left behind. Then soon into Richmond Park. Here is a vision, entering Roehampton Gate, on a fair morning, not to be obtained from your bedroom ceiling. Let your eye roam over the scenery and endeavour to store all its beauties. It is all yours. We tread the paths towards Richmond admiring, possibly, en route the horsemen and women and their steeds. Perhaps these do not attract, then there are deer who gaze gently at you possibly wondering to themselves "Who are these queer people?" If we are fortunate they will stage a contest for us, and the sight of two young stags engaged in a head to head fight with an old member standing by, referee fashion, to see fair play, and the herd in audience, is not lightly to be passed by. We press on, and soon Richmond hoves in sight. The view from the Hill is famous. Down into the town, across the river, and on to Twickenham; then shortly into Bushey Park by the famous long walk and its avenue of chestnuts. Minds go back to their planter, William of Orange, and we agree that the aspect is "not too bad." Out of the Park at the end of the avenue, and we face Hampton Court Palace. More history, in which Henry VIII is the "star turn." We decide to enter the grounds and admire, in season, the crocus, the Dutch trees, the famous clock and possibly the fair visitors. The maze is barred. Eventually we pass through the Home Park and emerge by Kingston Bridge. Here if you wish you may cut your stroll short and ride, but far better carry on and by the main road back to Putney Bridge. The time will now be 2 o'clock Away for home. You will probably be able to eat well and possibly sleep. Satisfying enough and infinitely better than pottering around at home or wandering about to kill time. And, mark you well, your "finish" on the track next season will be stronger as a result of your Strolls (not Stroll). So shall we repeat the continuous performance? Stroll, Sunday morning next, meet Putney Bridge, South Side, at 10 a.m W.H.H. items.s: ABANDONED. Notes that the third triangular contest with T.V.H. and Ashcombe was abandoned for a frozen course, that Boxing Day entries rose to 75, and that the Boxing Day Godstone walk was postponed to April 14th. Our well-filled fixture list does not permit the postponement of the third of the triangular contests with T.V.H. and Ashcombe A C, and so owing to a frozen course we had to content ourselves with a training spin over Feltham roads. There were nine more entries than last year for our Boxing Day events, making 75. What a pity the sprinters cannot raise a gallop the day after Christmas! They were the only department to go back on last year's numbers. It was hoped that by now we should be singing the praises of our distance men, but owing to the "seasonable weather," the Boxing Day Godstone walk was postponed until April 14th. Feltham Godstone T.V.H. Ashcombe A C

items.label: January 1928
items.sum: Running notes urging the team towards the South of the Thames and Southern Championships, and announcing forthcoming fixtures and socials.
items.s: RUNNING. Running notes urging the team towards the South of the Thames and Southern Championships, and announcing forthcoming fixtures and socials. Our best position in the South of the Thames Championship since the war, was fifth in 1926. Although we had good reason to expect something better last year, we were eighth and disappointed. In this race, there is the "Coleman Cup" for the first club to finish every man of its team of twelve. It is within our powers to win this trophy. A fortnight later comes the Southern Championship. A different proposition this, as the distance jumps from 7 to 10 miles. Among the "possibles" for our team we have a likely winner, and now, team men, is your chance to earn laurels. RUN! RUN!! RUN!!! Run as if the Devil himself were chasing you! You can do it if you try. Think of the kudos you are likely to gain—not for yourself—but for your CLUB. And DON'T pack up—not even if your are twelfth man, not even if you do cast a shoe, get leg-weary, sick or contract any other horrible or impossible complaint, for now is YOUR chance to make history. Remember that in getting your place in the team you are ousting another member who is perhaps even more keen than you to run. We can win the Cup given for the club with headquarters in Surrey to finish its twelve men first. Do you remember what happened last year? The twelfth man gave up—with what result? Why, if he had walked the last lap to finish last we should have won this cup with shoals of points in hand! So don't forget, Mr. Twelfth-man, you are as important in this competition as the winner. Forthcoming attractions.—January 21st. Social run at Rosehill, Sutton with Mitcham A C. Tea and social evening, during which the Inter-Club Relay Shield will be presented to us, at the White Hart, Mitcham The "Summer" runners, so interested in the relay competitions, will find it worth while to come along with their lady friends.
