items.sum: Report of the 22 January inter-club fixtures: a walk with Surrey W.C. from Croydon and a 7 mile run at home against Mitcham A.C. and the Irish Guards, won by Belgrave.
items.s: INTER-CLUB RACES. Report of the 22 January inter-club fixtures: a walk with Surrey W.C. from Croydon and a 7 mile run at home against Mitcham A.C. and the Irish Guards, won by Belgrave. January 22nd, produced an atrocious day for our two Inter-Club fixtures. The walkers being at Croydon for the race with the Surrey W.C. whilst the runners were at home to Mitcham A.C. and the Irish Guards. Over a course of 11¾ miles to Banstead and back 9 walkers had their enthusiasm sorely tested by snow and ice bound roads but were not dismayed and put up quite a respectable show. The Club received the usual and expected beating but in H. F. King supplied the first man home in very fast time having regard to the conditions prevailing. The runners, however, over the 7 mile course, added to their team victories with a score of 54 points to the 109 of Mitcham and 158 of the Irish Guards, who had first man home in J. Ingram. A special word of thanks is due to those who turned out as pointsmen At any time this job is no joy trip but on such a day it was most uninviting. To add to the troubles, one runner got lost and when all others had dressed and the "lost sheep" still had not returned it was necessary to call for volunteers to form a search party. Ken O'Kell, Bayliss and Button promptly responded and treked over the Common, dismal and damp, in an effort to trace him. No light undertaking especially after having raced 7 miles. Fortunately nothing serious had happened and eventually the lost one turned up after having been out nearly 3 hours. H. F. King H. F. King first man home in the inter-club walk with Surrey W.C. J. items.s: CLUB NOTES. The Hon. Secretary's club notes: payment for the Gazette, County colours for Footer and Cook, news of members, a new walker, the Surrey road walk trophy, the Sheffield trip and the Brighton relay. The last number of the Belgravian seems to have met with general approval judging by the congratulations received from our members and other well wishers. Some of our members have got the idea that this publication is issued FREE. I would ask all those to look on the front page and then forward the amount to our Hon. Editor and so relieve him from anxiety as to the expence of publishing the Gazette. * * * Our Editor from his Uneasy chair has given you all the details to date of the different races that have been held since our last number was issued so there is no need for me to go over these except to congratulate all who have done their utmost to keep the Club colors flying. * * * We have to offer congratulations to H. E. Footer and H. S. Cook who have been awarded County Colors for the Cross Country Championship. They will represent Surrey at Chesham on January 29th. * * * I have received letters from our members F. Rickards, E A. Wall and C. H. Speechley I am pleased to announce that Rickards will start at once training for the National Road Walking Championship and Wall has a feeling that he would like to do some training as soon as the weather improves. He informs me that he has quite recovered from his serious illness but does not want to take any chances during the cold spell. * * * Members will no donbt be pleased to hear that Mr. T. W. Green has joined our walking section and is a first claim member. He will greatly strengthen our team. * * * The Surrey County Road Walking Championship will be held on March 26th. A cup presented by Sir Jeremiah Coleman to the S C.A.A. has been allocated to this race. Now then the walkers you have got to be the first holders of this trophy. Our host the genial William will not mind keeping it clean. It has been suggested to me that William will have to go on our list of officers as the Keeper of the Plate. * * * Arrangements have been published for our trip to Sheffield on March 5th, in pursuit of "Junior Championship" honours. Members and friends wishing to support the teams are requested to make early application so as seats can be booked on the Special Train. * * * Our President is getting more and more respect showered upon him. The number of dinners that he is now compelled to eat shatters any idea of his taking to serious training again. The committee like Curzon Bros., will have to take extreme measures * * * At the time of writing these notes nothing has been settled as to the Club's entry in the News of the World Brighton Relay Race. We shall no doubt have to run in a trial race to secure a place in the actual race. Will all of you bear this in mind and do a little extra bit of training. The Club should not have been called upon to run in this trial if all the members in the last race had run up to their form. H. E. Footer H. E. items.sum: Report of the club's Annual Dinner at Stanleys Restaurant, Clapham Junction, on 14 January, chaired by the President R. W. Ricketts.
items.s: ANNUAL DINNER. Report of the club's Annual Dinner at Stanleys Restaurant, Clapham Junction, on 14 January, chaired by the President R. W. Ricketts. The Annual Dinner was held at Stanleys Restaurant, Clapham Junction on January 14th, with our President, R. W. Ricketts in the chair. If it may be regretted that the attendance was below that of last year it cannot be disputed that in all other respects the gathering was a great success and a credit to the work of our Social Hon. Sec. and his Sub. Committee. In proposing the toast of "The Club," the President was able to refer to our recent County success and to a general feeling of satisfaction and optimism among all for our future prospects. Our Assistant Hon Sec. responded, and whilst speaking of the progress and prospects of many of our active members emphasised the desire for the support of those who, whilst having to a great extent passed their racing careers, could still render much help and to the Club in so many other ways. Mr. W. Griffin proposed the toast to "The Visitors," replied to jointly by Messrs. W. J. Pepper and J. Binks. Mr. E Gordon briefly and ably proposed the toast of "The Chairman" which was given feelingly with musical honours and vociferous cheers. The musical entertainment, in spite of difficulties caused by last moment alterations due to the prevailing complaint, was really excellent and much appreciated. R. W. Ricketts R. W. items.s: GAZETTE FUND. Appeal from the Hon. Editor for members to subscribe to the Gazette fund, with thanks to H. Evans for a Christmas cake raffled for the fund. The Hon. Editor wishes to remind members that "The Belgravian" makes a big demand on the Club funds and can only be continued by the support of all. To those who have always tendered assistance and support our best thanks and appreciation are recorded. To those who have so far failed to render their share, and to those new members to whom we have not yet appealed, we wish to state that if all who received the Gazette would subscribe to the fund we should be enabled to issue more often that at present and at a reduced figure to that which appears on Page 1. May we have your assistance. ? A special acknowledgement of thanks is due to Mr. H. Evans for again presenting a Gigantic Christmas Cake, which, raffled on behalf of The Fund, produced a sum of £1 10s. 6d. H. Evans Mr. H. Evans presented a Christmas cake raffled for the Gazette fund

items.s: ANSWERS TO CORRESPONDENTS. Humorous mock answers from the Editor to correspondents writing under pen-names. The Editor takes no responsibility for the accuracy of all his replies, nor does he reply by post. If your answer does not appear below, buy the next issue. A "Long" Sufferer. I do not give medical advice, but in your case for ingrowing toe nail I would advise you to have the toe removed. The nail will then not grow. Any licensed slaughter-house man should remove the toe at a small charge. Dunk. Sorry to hear that you experience difficulty in running in our "overcoats." The matter will receive attention, which should take a load off your mind. Airman. Many thanks for offers of lessons in the Charleston. Think however that this is best left alone. Appears dangerous in more than one respect as you probably know. Belfry. Congratulations. Do not consider however that Slide Rules and Logarithm Tables should be supplied to handicappers. I much prefer the "hand-in-the-cap" method personally. Chef Thanks. Have your "Dog Yards" any relation to the "Dog Watches" as known at sea. ? Sunlight. Thanks for letter. Glad to hear of your re-grading. Have read with pleasure your Horoscope. I should advise you to take care of the dark woman with the red garters who will cross your path. False teeth should not be sent out they should be washed at home. Blood Mixture. Your letter and explanation to hand. Thanks for correcting us. After a consideration I think that Tobys might be taken as a Medicine. My medical adviser suggests that I want a change so try a case on me. Nunc est Bibendum.
